title: If statements and blocks
recap: An if statement controls exactly one statement, but a block groups several statements so one condition can control all of them. Braces after the condition make the group explicit and avoid dangling-else surprises.
An if / else if / else chain selects the first matching branch. Blocks keep each branch readable and make it obvious which statements belong to which condition.
objectives: Group several statements under one if condition with a block.
Chain conditions with else if and finish with else.
Exercise every branch with deterministic calls.
warnings: Without a block, only the first statement after the condition belongs to the if.
A dangling else binds to the nearest unmatched if; blocks remove the ambiguity.
Do not print the same line from multiple branches.
challenge: Complete printGrade so a score of 90 or above prints the grade A line and a distinction status line inside one block, a score of 80 or above prints the grade B line, and anything lower prints the C-or-lower line. Keep all three calls in main.
hints: The distinction status is a second statement inside the first block.
Chain the second condition with else if (score >= 80).
The final else handles every remaining score.
